pr_title: Preserving line endings in blockinfile module
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
Preserve line endings in blockinfile module.

Fixes #64966

##### ISSUE TYPE
<!--- Pick one below and delete the rest -->
- Bugfix Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
blockinfile

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
I'm not sure if this is the desired way to fix this ... it looks kinda "hacky", but OTOH allows us to remove other hacks (e.g. fixing new lines at the end of files).

In #65677 it was suggested the changed line endings might be related to missing `newline=''` parameter when calling `open()`. But trying to add this you get the following error: `ValueError: binary mode doesn't take a newline argument`. Instead it looks like `splitlines()` is the actual culprit ... at least in this case. :neutral_face:

issue_context.title: Ansible blockinfile ^M bug!?
issue_context.body:
### SUMMARY
In SuSe SLES there is a file: /etc/vimrc. It contains ^M characters, like in line:  101 containing:
    map! <ESC>OM  ^M
When running module blockinfile on this file it removes the ^M characters.
The blockinfile just needs to adds some lines on the end of the file. Even when the lines are already there it removes the ^M characters.

It looks like that it reads the file and cannot handle the ^M characters and writes the buffer without the characters to the file.

needs_info

I'm going to hazard a guess that this is still an issue, due to `.splitlines()` in python translating windows newlines into unix newlines, and stripping them.

Simply using `.readlines()` will also translate.

It looks like to get around it, you need to use `io.open` with `newlines=''` and `.readlines()` to prevent universal newline translation.  But this will require a rewrite in that we would need to change the assumption that the lines don't contain the newline.

We then run into a problem with us using unix newlines to be inserted, and what happens if there are multiple newline types in a single file?

review_comments: This code ensured that the block text always had a line separator after it. With this removed, a block that has no line separator ends up being concatenated to the end mark.
